requirement:
`Validation::validate` works without a configured model provider. A callback
that never invokes the agent interface does not fail because no agent is configured.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. `Validation::validate` must work when no model provider is configured, and a callback that never invokes the agent interface must not fail because no agent is configured.

The test `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/validation.rs#fn[runner_reuses_negative_judgments_and_records_only_callback_observations]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It builds `Validator::new(&graph, |_| Ok("v1".into()))` with no `with_agent` call, so no agent is configured. The `Memory` callback `impl[Memory/Validation]/fn[validate]` runs here with the default `Memory` settings, so it never calls `ctx.ask`. The test then does the following:
- It calls `validate_node(&9).await.unwrap()` twice, so a `NoAgentConfigured` error would fail the unwrap. It asserts the result is `false`, which matches the callback's `node != 9` rule.
- It asserts that the callback ran (`started == [9]`) and stored a record. The record has no reads, no selections and no dependencies, so the run did not touch an agent.
- It calls `check_node` and checks the `Current`, `Missing` and `Stale` states, and it runs a second validator `v2` that also has no agent. All of these also succeed without a provider.

The related test `runner_does_not_store_a_missing_agent_error_and_supports_intermediate_calls` is the contrast case. When the callback does ask for the agent and none is configured, the result is `NoAgentConfigured`. This confirms that the failure appears only on agent use, so the no-agent success in the marked test is meaningful. Other tests, such as `concurrent_single_node_validations_keep_separate_traces`, also validate through agent-less validators.

I found no uncovered obligation, boundary or failure case in the requirement text.
